docs.title: SAFE4SOC Information Sharing Gateway
docs.text:
SAFE4SOC Information Sharing Gateway (S4S-IS-GW) The SAFE4SOC Information Sharing Gateway (S4S-IS-GW) is a cybersecurity software component developed within the European research and innovation project SAFE4SOC, funded under the EU Digital Europe Programme.

Its primary purpose is to enable secure, interoperable, and automated exchange of cybersecurity information between different organizations and security infrastructures, particularly Security Operations Centers (SOCs).

The gateway acts as an intermediary between cybersecurity systems, allowing them to exchange security alerts and incident-related information while enforcing configurable security and information-sharing policies.

docs.title: Key objectives
docs.text:
1. Interoperability: Facilitate standardized cybersecurity information exchange using the Incident Detection Message Exchange Format version 2 (IDMEFv2).
  2. Secure communication: Protect exchanged information through encrypted communication and mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication.
  3. Information filtering: Apply configurable policies to determine which cybersecurity information may be shared with other organizations.
  4. Data validation: Validate exchanged security alerts against predefined JSON schemas to ensure structural correctness and interoperability.
  5. Integration: Connect existing SOC infrastructures and security monitoring systems without requiring major changes to their internal architectures.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The gateway consists of a sender gateway on the sender side and the receiving gateway on the receiver side. As database for storing the received alert messages Kafka is used. Kafka does not natively support JSON objects send via HTTP REST, therefore a translation was provided by the Kafka developers to translate HTTP Rest API calls into native Kafka protocol communication.

The sender gateway receives IDMEFv2 as JSON formatted alert message via HTTP message. The gateway sender afterward performs configured filtering or enrichment and forwards the alert to the receiver side gateway. Here the alert is also filtered or enriched as configured and afterward sent to the Kafka HTTP Rest API container. The Kafka REST API container does the translation to the final destination, the Kafka database which is locally reachable on the receiver side.

docs.title: Compilation
docs.text: The project is configured for the IDE Intellij Community Edition. Is uses GraalVM to produce an executable with faster startup times and less memory footprint during execution.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: To create the image, run the following goal. NOTE: GraalVM 22.3+ is required. For installation instructions please see - Docker and docker-compose must be installed beforehand - Install GraalVM https://www.graalvm.org/latest/getting-started/ - Install gcc glibc-devel zlib-devel etc. https://www.graalvm.org/latest/reference-manual/native-image/

docs.title: Building Instructions
docs.text:
In main project's path run 

./gradlew clean nativeCompile
Then a binary is compiled which is later used for the docker build. The compilation time takes about 5 minutes on a modern laptop. You can do a test of the app as follows (expect missing configuration issues at this stage): 
build/native/nativeCompile/s4sgateway
Then, you can build the docker container image: 
docker build -t s4sgateway .
Testing keystores must be available for propper configuration which must be created by calling: 
cd pki-test
./generate-mtls-certs.sh
cd ..
Once the image was built these commands can launch the kafka services and the gateways Launching kafka. 
docker compose up -d rest-proxy control-center schema-registry broker
docker compose up -d gateway-receiver gateway-sender
Launching gateway-sender (separate console recommended) 
docker compose up gateway-sender
Launching gateway-receiver (separate console recommended) 
docker compose up gateway-receiver

If all services are up and running the gateways can be tested, please see the next sections.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The gateway must be configured using the file application.properties. A different version of this file is used for a gateway taking either the sender or receiver role, respectively the files: - application.properties (for debugging directly in IntelliJ IDE) - receiver.properties - sender.properties - docker.properties (for launch via docker-compose script.)

The files are mapped into the corresponding docker container via docker-compose.yaml. Please edit config in docker-compose file as otherwise the config will be overwritten.

The following entries must be specified for the gateway in sender mode: 

gatewayRole=SENDER
This switch lets the gateway act as sending gateway. Options are either SENDER or RECEIVER. 
relevantHeaders={'content-type','accept','user-Agent','accept-Encoding','safe4soc-receiver-hostname','safe4soc-receiver-port'}
This array lists headers to be forwarded within the gateway. All other headers are dropped.

docs.title: Sender Gateway Properties
docs.text:
gatewayDomainRC=localhost
gatewayPortRC=8081
These entries specify the destination domain and port of the receiving gateway where messages must be forwarded to.

gatewayDomainSD=localhost
gatewayPortSD=8080
These entries specify self-information for the gateway, needed for alert entry enrichment, for instance.

docs.title: Receiver Gateway Properties
docs.text:
kafkaDomainLocal=kafkalocal
kafkaPortLocal=8082
These entries identify where the local kafka database can be found.

docs.title: SSL Activation or Deactivation (DEBUG Connection Settings)
docs.text:
The gateway has a setting to control the inbound SSL configuration (Spring boot VM settings), and the outbound SSL configuration (Java internal SSL Context object). Both can be activated or deactivated separately using the following flags in docker-compose.

      GATEWAY_PROTOCOL: https     # for communication from gateway sender to gateway receiver
      SSL_INBOUND_ACTIVATED: true
      SSL_OUTBOUND_ACTIVATED: true

For debug purposes in a testing environment the SSL-settings can be both be set to false. This means that neither the initial connection from the outside inside the Gateway-sender nor the forwarding from Gateway-sender to Geteway-receiver will apply HTTPS but only HTTP, which is of course not acceptable for a production environment but ONLY FOR TESTING PURPOSES! The file docker-compose-debug-http.yaml is properly configured to work out of the box and can be launched using:

docker compose up -d rest-proxy control-center schema-registry broker 
docker compose -f docker-compose-debug-http.yaml up gateway-sender
docker compose -f docker-compose-debug-http.yaml up gateway-receiver

docs.title: Information Sharing Agreement Configuration
docs.text:
The entry about the ISA is important, as it also contains the config about necessary filtering and enrichment instructions. Please note: JSON objects across multiple lines must be formatted with \ at the end of each line is the properties files.

isaConfig=\
{\
  "provider_reason": "compliance",\
  "intended_use": "alert_gathering",\
  "data_usage_policies": {\
    "use_until": "2024-12-12",\
    "use_after": "2024-09-12",\
    "share_further": "false"\
  },\
  "data_sender_SIEM_brand": "Example Company A",\
  "data_sender_SIEM_version": "Version 0.1",\
  "IDMEFv2_attributes": {\
    "attributes_to_transmit": [],\
    "attributes_to_neglect": [],\
    "attributes_to_anonymize": [],\
    "attributes_to_pseudonemize": []\
  },\
  "sending_mode": "",\
  "encryption_requirements": [],\
  "authentication_requirements": [],\
  "connection_requirements": [],\
The basic attributes above were derived from the requirements specified and might be frequently adapted in meaning and structure.

  "filterConfig": {\
    "Version": "",\
    "ID": "",\
    "Status": "",\
    "OrganisationName": "",\
    "CreateTime": "",\
    "StartTime": "",\
    "Cause": "",\
    "Category": "",\
    "Priority": "",\
    "Confidence": "",\
    "Description": "",\
    "Analyzer": {\
      "IP": "",\
      "Name": "",\

      "Type": "",\
      "Model": "",\
      "Category": "",\
      "Data": "",\
      "Method": "",\
      "GeoLocation": "",\
      "UnLocation": "",\
      "Location": ""\
    },\
    "Sensor": "",\
    "Source": {\
      "IP": "",\
      "Protocol": ""\
    },\
    "Target": ""\
  },\
The Filtering configuration uses a nested list in JSON format. If identifiers for key value pairs are found, the entry's content is replaced with an empty string (""). If identifiers for nested objects are found, either the complete object is cleaned, when no sub-entries were given, or only the sub entries mentioned are replaced with blank spaces or empty arrays, depending on the element. The list above is an example of a configuration which filters all entries.

  "enrichmentConfig": {\
    "CreateTime": "",\
    "StartTime": ""\
  }\
}
The enrichment configuration uses a nested list in JSON format, also. However, each enrichment functionality must be implemented specifically. The class Utils contains a prepared nested case structure for all elements to individually implement an enrichment where necessary.

docs.title: Configuring the Filtering for IDMEFv2
docs.text:

docs.title: Demonstration
docs.text:
To fully demonstrate how alerts are sent to Kafka through the gateway following commands are necessary. The Kafka github project provides docker samples for all their services running out the box. Their sample was taken from here: https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/get-started/platform-quickstart.html. The docker sample was taken from here: https://github.com/confluentinc/cp-all-in-one/tree/7.9.0-post/cp-all-in-one/docker-compose.yml

The gateways were added to the docker compose file located in the root folder of the project. It can be launched via: 

docker-compose up -d rest-proxy control-center schema-registry broker gateway-receiver gateway-sender
Please note more services are included in the sample file, such as flink or ksqldb but for the demo they are not needed.

After about a minute the system should be launched and the Kafka dashboard can be reached via web browser at 

localhost:9021
You should see something similar to this: Landing page

Click on controlcenter.cluster

Click on Topics

Click on alerts (if it was already set up correctly). If it is not there yet you can either send the first message via curl or click on the GUI "Add topic" at the top right.

Click on messages to see the current stored messages.

Please note that for Kafke message consumption each message requires a key, in this case it was "test" and the IDMEFv2 alert is stored inside the value filed of the JSON message. It is also possible to specify a JSON schema for the correct format of the messages, but for this demo it is not required. Please note that the Kafka rest proxy cannot process IDMEFv2 alerts directly but requires an envelope using a JSON record array and a key and value object as shown below.

docs.title: Compilation of Project Documentation
docs.text:
Use these commands to update the documentation

docker compose -f docker-compose.docs.yml run --rm mkdocs build
The resulting files are placed in site/.

docs.title: Automatically publish to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
Create .github/workflows/documentation.yml: 

name: Publish Documentation

on:
push:
branches:
- main
paths:
- "docs/**"
- "mkdocs.yml"
- ".github/workflows/documentation.yml"
workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
contents: write

jobs:
deploy:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install MkDocs
        run: pip install "mkdocs-material==9.*"

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        run: mkdocs gh-deploy --force

This builds the documentation and pushes the generated website to the gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
This section details how alerts can be sent through the gateways.

The gateways can be tested using a postman collection, one for either a secured gateway or an insecure configured gateway using http for development purposes. Get postman here: https://www.postman.com/downloads/ Once installed the testing collection (SAFE4SOC.postman_collection.json) which contains predefined REST API requests can be imported via File -> Import.

The following sections show sample usages of the API using curl and command-line only.
